attribution.note: Marcus wrote this on his own Substack, in the first person, about his own book.

semantics.note: The claim that can be checked is retrospective: his 2024 book contained this warning. The draft keeps his 'probably' about the LLM link and treats the tariff episode as his framing, not as something asserted as fact.

contract.note: Treating the sentence as a paraphrase, and reading it as a warning about poorly judged LLM use with broad consequences, is a fair and ordinary plain reading. The contract rightly leaves out whether an LLM wrote the tariff formula.

evidence.note: An authentic 2024 excerpt from the book raises concern about consequential, biased uses of LLMs, such as job decisions. This support is weak: it asks whether harm occurred rather than warning outright that LLMs would be misused.

An independent 2024 review says the book warns about publishers sharing poorly vetted AI-generated news and about overreliance on AI in critical infrastructure with catastrophic consequences. This matches the warning Marcus describes.
This is Marcus's own post. It shows how he framed the tariff episode, but it cannot prove what the book said.

reviews.rationale: An independent review (e2) and a book excerpt (e1) show that Taming Silicon Valley (2024) warned about careless deployment of generative AI and text-generating systems with widespread consequences, such as poorly vetted AI news and overreliance in critical infrastructure. That meets the support condition. No counterevidence was found. The full book was not inspected, but the excerpt and review are enough to establish the warning. Whether an LLM shaped the tariff formula is not assessed here.
